newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Perry says U.S. watching northern Iraq closely.
newsitem.headline: Perry says U.S. watching northern Iraq closely.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Thursday he was watching the situation in northern Iraq closely and hoped there would be no reason to use U.S. military power against President Saddam Hussein's forces again.
He was speaking after Kurdish chieftain Massoud Barzani threatened to ask the Iraqi government for further help in his feud with a rival Kurdish militia.

Perry said there was no indication so far that Iraqi forces were moving against Kurds in northern Iraq, a step that resulted in U.S. cruise missile attacks against Baghdad's air defences in southern Iraq last month.
"We continue to have substantial military forces in the area. I sincerely hope that there will be no need to use those forces," Perry, who is visiting Russia, told reporters in response to questions.
Fighting broke out again last week between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq and some reports from the area suggested that Iraqi military forces might be preparing to intervene.

"We are watching that very, very closely. The evidence to this point is inconclusive," Perry said. "Nothing that has happened so far would suggest to me that they (U.S. military forces) would need to be used."

U.S. warships and B-52 bombers fired cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq last month after Iraqi troops attacked Kurds in the north. The troops later withdrew and Iraq has since largely rebuilt its air defences.

Perry said on Wednesday that he and Army General John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. military Joint Chiefs of Staff, were reviewing intelligence almost every day but had so far not seen any immediate danger to U.S. and allied pilots flying protective missions over a southern Iraq "no fly" zone.
